editorial.headline: Textile Finished-Goods Wholesale: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale of finished textile goods is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration.
editorial.body:
**For a foreign investor considering Bali, the decisive fact comes first: this activity cannot be registered for PMA there today.** The barrier does not come from a national foreign-ownership limit. At national level, it is open to PMA, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali reaches a different outcome because the activity is blocked under the province’s moratorium. This is not a secondary caveat added to an otherwise straightforward national position: it determines whether a PMA registration can be made in Bali. National openness does not create a Bali registration route.

The activity is wholesale trade in finished products of the textile industry. Its stated scope gives that phrase real edges: rope and cordage; textile carpets and rugs; sacks; varied knitted goods; fur goods; umbrellas and parasols; tarpaulins; ship sails; and parachutes. These are the kinds of textile-industry output traded at wholesale, already in finished form. The listed articles show the reach of the activity from ropes and carpeting to tarpaulins, ship sails and parachutes. Each example is named in the scope itself, making the perimeter of the activity concrete.

Who can register nationally? The record opens the activity to Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. That all-scale availability belongs to the national position and should not be read as an exception to Bali’s rule. In Bali, the decisive condition is risk: at the Large scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA in those risk classes, and the record connects this activity’s block to that moratorium in May 2026. That is why the Large-scale risk assessment has a broader consequence for the Bali registration result stated here. Hence the clear, two-layer conclusion: a 100% foreign stake is permitted nationally, but PMA registration in Bali is blocked today.

The national PMA position is recorded under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The Bali restriction is separately tied to the provincial rule described in the record, not to a lower national ownership percentage. Neither layer cancels the other: they answer different parts of the same registration question.
